sections.h2: What towns and cities make up Barrow County?
sections.html:
Barrow County lies in east central Georgia on the edge of the Atlanta metro area, and Winder is its seat. Voters approved the amendment that created it on November 3, 1914, using pieces of Gwinnett, Jackson and Walton counties; it became the state's 149th county of what are now 159 (Wikipedia).

It is a small county by area, 163 square miles with 160 of them land, and all of it drains into the Upper Oconee River sub-basin of the Altamaha River basin. Gwinnett lies to the west, Walton to the south, Oconee to the southeast, Jackson to the east and Hall to the north; Clarke County meets it at a single point.

  • Cities: Auburn, Statham and Winder
  • Towns: Bethlehem, Braselton (mostly Jackson County, partly Gwinnett and Hall) and Carl
  • Census-designated place: Russell
  • Unincorporated: Barrow Heights, Mulberry and Whistleville

Since Braselton spans several counties, a Braselton owner should read the parcel record to see which county's tax commissioner sends the bill.

sections.h2: How quickly has Barrow County added people and houses?
sections.html:
Very quickly. The census counted 21,354 residents in 1980, 46,144 in 2000, 69,367 in 2010 and 83,505 in 2020, and QuickFacts estimates 99,773 for mid-2025. The 2020 count showed 30,019 housing units and 28,727 households, 38.8% of them with children, and a median age of 36.4.

Compare the 1,584 permits with the 14 in Bacon County and the picture is clear: Barrow County is still building. QuickFacts lists 518.5 people per square mile, against 39.2 in Bacon County, and 78.5% of housing units are owner-occupied. In the 2020 count, 67.0% of residents lived in urban areas, 77.4% of occupied units were owned, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 1.5%. A seller in a newer subdivision near Winder or Auburn will be listed beside many similar houses, so price and condition carry extra weight.

sections.h2: Which school cluster serves a Barrow County address?
sections.html:
Barrow County Schools is the sole district, and its schools group into two clusters named for Winder-Barrow High School and Apalachee High School. A buyer's school assignment depends on the cluster serving the address.

  • Winder-Barrow: Winder-Barrow High, Richard B. Russell Middle, Bear Creek Middle, and Holsenbeck, Bramlett, Statham, County Line and Winder elementary schools
  • Apalachee: Apalachee High, Westside Middle, Haymon-Morris Middle, and Auburn, Kennedy, Bethlehem and Yargo elementary schools
  • Also listed: Barrow Arts and Sciences Academy

This list comes from Wikipedia, so confirm attendance zones with the district before naming a school in a listing.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value in Barrow County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner works from 30 N. Broad Street, Winder, GA 30680. The Barrow County Tax Portal gives (770) 307-3106 and weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30. Card payments carry a 2.5% service fee, minimum $1.50. The portal also says vehicle transactions require a Georgia driver's license or ID card with a Barrow County address.

Values are the Tax Assessors Office's job, at the same street address, and the county invites calls between 8 and 5 on weekdays. Notices can be printed from qPublic. The commissioner picks the due date and mails the bill but has no say over your value.

sections.h2: When do Barrow County notices and bills arrive?
sections.html:
The county's 2024 release said real property and personal property notices (aircraft, boats, business equipment) went out May 1, while final tax bills would wait until September and fall due in November. Treat that as the normal rhythm, and rely on the date on your own bill.

A notice is not a bill. It estimates tax from the assessed value. If you disagree, you have 45 days to appeal, either online through qPublic, by mail, or in person at the Tax Assessors Office.

  • Permitted grounds: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption
  • Tracks: Board of Equalization, hearing officer or arbitrator
  • State revenue officials cannot override a board, hearing officer, arbitrator or court on one parcel

sections.h2: What can I look up online before listing a Barrow County house?
sections.html:
Two sites cover most of it. The tax portal lets you search information on any property in the county, pay property tax and renew car tags online. The assessors' qPublic pages let you print the current and prior year assessment notices from the assessment section, which helps when a buyer's agent asks what the value was last year.

Pay attention to the returned-check rule on the tax portal: if a bank dishonors your check, a service fee is assessed under state law, and the county uses Envision Payment Solutions for recovery, reachable at 1-877-290-5460. For a closing, a certified payment avoids that problem.

The county's own notice adds that the assessors will answer questions about an assessment notice or the appeal process by phone on weekdays, so a seller who expects a challenge can start that conversation before the 45 days run out.

sections.h2: Can a city also bill me inside Barrow County?
sections.html:
Possibly. A parcel inside a city may be taxed by the city as well as the county, so ask the city clerk whether a separate bill exists. With three cities and three towns here, never assume a county payoff covers any municipal balance.

Georgia's revenue department says the owner on January 1 answers for the whole year's tax even if the house sells on January 2, and no refund is allowed for part of a year. The title company should request a current payoff from each billing office and settle both at closing.

If an earlier year is unpaid, the tax commissioner's office can say whether a lien was recorded.

sections.h2: What becomes of surplus money after a Barrow County tax sale?
sections.html:
Barrow County's real property page says it works with Weissman Excess Funds Management on surplus from tax sales. The firm publishes open records on the funds it handles, typically refreshed on the 1st and 15th of each month, and you request information by email.

The page states plainly that Barrow County does not release excess funds to third parties. Someone who lost property to a tax sale should contact the Tax Commissioner's Office or the firm directly about a claim, rather than pay a stranger to chase it.

sections.h2: Where do Barrow County homestead applications go?
sections.html:
Georgia gives a standard homestead exemption to owners who live in the home as their primary residence, and many counties add richer local ones. The state says applications go to the county tax commissioner or the assessors, depending on the county.

Phone (770) 307-3106 to learn which Barrow County office takes yours, and bring proof of residency. After the exemption is subtracted from assessed value, the millage rate is applied to what remains.

faqs.q: Where is the Barrow County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: At 30 N. Broad Street in Winder, GA 30680. Call (770) 307-3106 on weekdays between 8:00 and 4:30.

faqs.q: Does a Barrow County assessment notice require payment?
faqs.a: No, it is an estimate of tax based on assessed value, not a bill. Final bills follow later, in September according to the county's 2024 announcement.

faqs.q: What is the way to appeal a Barrow County value?
faqs.a: Act within 45 days of the notice. Appeals may be filed online through qPublic, by mail, or at the Tax Assessors Office at 30 N. Broad Street.

faqs.q: Are tax sale surplus funds paid out to third parties in Barrow County?
faqs.a: No. The county states that it does not release excess funds to third parties, and claims run through its Tax Commissioner's Office and excess funds partner.

faqs.q: Who pays if I sell a Barrow County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for the full year under Georgia law, with no part-year refund. Divide the bill with the buyer in your closing paperwork.
